P1.evidence: No setter pre-qualified this prospect — he booked directly off Instagram — so the read-back check does not apply. The frame was two-part and trailed off: 'what I would like to do, go over where you're at, where you want to go, see if we can help you' — no 'what's in the way' and no 'what you need'. No frame agreement was requested, and no open question was asked; the prospect simply started talking about the Instagram account at 00:01:03.

P2.evidence: Nutrition was the standout — a full day-in-the-life run-through plus the off-track probe, 'what's your go-to off-track thing?', which surfaced sugar three times a week and occasional beers. Injuries were properly asked: 'there's nothing like stiffnesses, pains, aches, anything that we should know about?' Body fat was asked ('what is it at the moment, do you think?') but age, height and weight were all volunteered unprompted at 00:08:55 and 00:03:00 and so score as partial. Occupation was volunteered — 'I manage a big group of companies for almost 400 people' — and never asked, nor was desk-bound versus on-feet. No health-conditions question, no sleep question (bedtime only surfaced inside the food timeline), no energy question.

P3.evidence: The surface layer ran well — 'how does that peak for you specifically look like?' produced the Brad Pitt in Fight Club target, and mobility, leanness and volume were each pinned down. The bridge to why also ran, and well: 'You already are in good shape. Why do you want to go to that next level? There are so many 41-year-olds that would sign for something like this.' The reflect-back landed: 'You just want to constantly reach new heights for yourself... It's just who you are.' But the depth stopped at identity. He learned there are two children aged two and four and did not use it — no 'who else does that impact', no route to family, marriage or legacy, and no 'something physical you want to do but can't'.

P4.evidence: The strongest phase of the call. Asked what he had tried ('you have done a good amount of fitness programs online'), what happened ('have they all been successful?'), why it did not stick ('why do you think that you're not able to reach that peak? What sort of stops you from doing that normally?') and the one blocker ('what's the one thing for you that we needed to solve in order to finally get to that peak?'). The prospect named the gap himself: 'putting the right amount of effort, but not just in terms of exercising, but exercising and nutrition.' The scripted 'the information isn't the problem' line never ran, and the final question was leading rather than open.

P5.evidence: No consequence frame was run. The rep asserted a fragment of one instead of asking for it — 'you always want to reach those next levels instead of staying stationary, because that's also where you go downhill' — but never asked what two more years of the same looks like, never asked whether he would settle for it, and never asked for a line in the sand. With a prospect whose whole pattern is a good result that stalls every summer, this was the available leverage and it was left on the table.

P6.evidence: P6a ran verbatim in substance: 'do you feel like if we get the workouts, the mobility, the nutrition, and that lifelong success aspect with Trevor in place, that you're going to finally reach that peak?' The answer was a hedge, not a yes — 'Hopefully, you know, like we say here in Morocco, we will do all the efforts and then if God wants.' The all-in question was only approximated ('do you feel like, yeah, let's get started?'), and the script's stop condition was ignored: the rep did not return to Phase 5 on hesitation, he went to price. That single decision explains the rest of the call.

P11.evidence: A close was attempted, so the phase applies, but no payment was collected and no link was sent — the call ended on 'probably tomorrow I'll get back to you'. Steps two through four could not be reached. The rep did correctly describe them when asked what happens next: 'we do that payment, then we get the meeting with Trevor booked in, and then I send you an onboarding form... and we would add you to the community' — describing is not doing.

objection_plays.detail: Trigger at 00:40:28, 'if you can give me some time to sleep on it'. Ran: the gut-feel probe ('what does your gut feeling at the moment say?'), the can-it-get-you-there test in its value form ('do you feel like that is worth 6K to you? Because if it wouldn't be, then I would say also don't do it'), and a sustained isolation down to the investment. Did not run: 'thinking isn't the problem, deciding is', 'the way you've been approaching this brought you here — when do you make a different decision?', 'that man you want to be, how does HE decide right now?', and the final 'are you sure, nothing else keeping you from being 100% in?'. He abandoned the play once the prospect restated his decision style and booked a callback instead.

The prospect said at 00:41:18 that he needed 'to discuss it with my family'. Not one move of OB ran — no 'money aside, do you personally feel this can get you there', no 'what obstacles might come up', no 'is there any reason she would not want you stronger', no ownership question. The rep did not acknowledge the family at all and continued isolating money. A second decision-maker entered the call and left unhandled.

Money was raised at 00:41:18. The rep ran the isolate reasonably well in two passes — 'is it that you are looking for other options because they might then be better or more so because of the investments?' and 'is it just a high amount that you have to invest in yourself... or is it more so that it's just not possible?' — establishing it was a discipline question, not a capacity question ('No, no, it's possible'). None of the financial-picture questions ran, which is defensible once capacity is confirmed. What replaced the play is the problem: he had already offered a $1,200 trial and interest-bearing instalments before the objection was properly isolated, so the structure preceded the diagnosis.

Two fear triggers. The back-injury concern at 00:20:19 was handled well but with mechanism explanation rather than the OE play, and it did resolve. The trust trigger at 00:37:07 — 'if you wire just this amount, you're not sure who you are working with' — got no OE move at all: no certainty reframe, no bridge, no plane, no burned-before. He answered a trust problem with a commercial concession, which leaves the doubt intact and the price reduced.

Script gap worth capturing. This prospect's objection was structural, not financial: he wanted to pay as he tested because he cannot verify a stranger over Zoom — 'it's always better if you can pay as you're going, as you're testing the method'. There is no scripted play for a prospect who can afford it, wants it, and simply will not wire a large sum to someone he has not verified. The absence of one is what pushed the rep into improvising a trial.

notes: Discovery and root-cause were genuinely good and the pillar delivery was thorough, but two decisions cost the call: he accepted 'hopefully, if God wants' as a commitment and went straight to price, and he answered a trust objection with a discount structure instead of a trust answer. Coach the P6 stop condition first — return to the consequence frame on any hedge — and give him a sanctioned response to 'I don't wire money to people I've just met' so he stops inventing trials.
